bib.title: Understanding Retrieval Augmentation for Long-Form Question Answering
bib.venue: Published as a conference paper at COLM 2024

question: How does retrieval augmentation (in-context evidence documents) change long-form answer generation by LMs, and how attributable are the generated answers to those documents?
contributions: Two controlled studies on LFQA: fix the LM and vary evidence documents, fix documents and vary LMs
SALAD: a dataset of sentence-level human attribution annotations (12k judgements over 4k answer sentences)
Evaluation of existing automatic attribution methods (NLI models, QAFactEval) on SALAD
Analysis of attribution patterns: document order effects, last-sentence unsupportedness, error types

method.summary: Prepend 3-4 evidence snippets (human, WebGPT, Bing, random) to an ELI5 question and sample long-form answers from GPT-3.5, Alpaca-7b and WebGPT. Measure surface statistics and have MTurk workers label each answer sentence Supported/Partially/Not Supported; then test NLI models and QAFactEval as automatic attribution judges.
method.task: long-form question answering with in-context retrieval; attribution evaluation

datasets.name: ELI5 (WebGPT test release)
datasets.split: test set released by WebGPT; 100 questions randomly sampled for manual attribution annotation
datasets.source: Fan et al. 2019 (Reddit ELI5); WebGPT outputs from Nakano et al. 2021

datasets.name: SALAD
datasets.size: 3,857 answer sentences with attribution labels (abstract: 12k human judgements over 4k sentences); 100 questions x 6 model-document configurations
datasets.split: three annotations per example, majority label; 3.4% discarded for no majority
datasets.source: collected on Amazon Mechanical Turk by the authors; released
datasets.preprocessing: Documents split into sentences; SimCSE similarity shown to annotators

datasets.name: Evidence document sets (Human, WebGPT, Bing, Random)
datasets.size: 3-4 snippets of roughly 100 words each; avg docs 3.5/3.5/4.0/3.5, avg words 308.9/388.0/400.0/388.0 (Human/WebGPT/Bing/Random)
datasets.source: Human and WebGPT from Nakano et al. 2021; Bing via Bing Search API v7.0; Random = WebGPT docs of another random test question
datasets.preprocessing: Bing: raw HTML processed with html2text and readability, split into 100-word segments, merged across top 10 pages, top four segments by BM25

models.name: WebGPT
models.architecture: GPT-3 fine-tuned to use Bing and compose LFQA answers

other.note: model not released; outputs taken from OpenAI answer viewer

other.selection: best by manual examination among GPT-J 6B, Flan-T5 11B, Llama 7B/13B/30B, Alpaca 7B

models.name: T5-11B NLI (Honovich et al. 2022)
models.architecture: T5 trained on MNLI, SNLI, FEVER, VitaminC

inference.samples: 3 answers per example per setting (for variability); WebGPT answers pre-generated
inference.prompting: Zero-shot instruction; documents line-separated and prepended to question
inference.retrieval: Not an end-to-end retriever: fixed document sets; Bing top-10 pages, BM25 selects top four 100-word segments; 3-4 snippets in context

parameters.nli_aggregation: max entailment over document-sentence/answer-sentence pairs; supported if score > threshold

metrics.name: Length
metrics.definition: number of sentences and words per answer

metrics.name: Self-BLEU
metrics.definition: lexical diversity; higher means more repetition

metrics.name: RankGen
metrics.definition: T5-XXL contrastive encoder score of answer as continuation of question prefix

metrics.name: Attribution label
metrics.definition: per-sentence Supported / Partially Supported / Not Supported w.r.t. evidence set (AIS framework)

metrics.name: F1 on detecting unsupported sentences
metrics.definition: micro-F1, Partially+Not Supported merged as positive class, per generation setting

eval.protocol: 3 MTurk annotators per sentence, majority vote, Krippendorff alpha 0.71; no significance tests stated; thresholds tuned on test data.

limits: Only ELI5 (one domain), 100 questions annotated, 3 samples per setting
Models are old: text-davinci-003, Alpaca-7b, WebGPT-175B (outputs only, not released); GPT-4 only in surface stats
Attribution is not factuality: a sentence unsupported by the given documents may still be true (authors note this)
NLI thresholds were tuned on the evaluation data itself, no dev set
Each LM was fed concatenated documents without positional manipulation beyond a shuffle control judged by the T5 model, not humans
Authors state their finding diverges from Krishna et al. 2021 and give possible reasons (low-relevance retrieval during their fine-tuning, ELI5 train-test overlap)
